message:
Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the clamped frame for the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) holds with margin because the demand is car-scale. The deciding demand is the factored frame design load (E36) of 12.3 kN, about one small car, carried on two transverse bearers in the bolted frame sketch (E37) with preloaded High Strength Friction Grip (HSFG, preloaded high-strength bolts) clamps, so slip does not govern.

Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the moving mass stays clear under crowd load because the shake is thumbnail-scale against the stop clearance. The deciding travel is the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm, giving 2.49 times margin to plus-minus 50.0 mm stops in the bolted frame sketch (E37), after the static weight of 4.90 kN from the TMD weight calculation (E35), about seven body weights, is already carried on the springs.

Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the retrofit stays hidden and serviceable while meeting comfort because all change is below deck with removable cover for re-tuning. The residual shaking is the TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m/s2, equal to 0.0556 times gravity like gentle bus braking, below the 1.00 m/s2 minimum-comfort bound. Ready, because load, clearance and access close jointly.
